ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
(Tracked-Changes Redline of Counterparty Draft)

Document Status: COUNSEL REDLINE — Incorporating Required Modifications and Insertions
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
Parties (as defined herein):
  Debtor: [Borrower / Account Holder] ("Debtor")
  Secured Party: [Administrative Agent], as Administrative Agent for the Lenders under the Credit Agreement ("Secured Party")
  Bank: [Depository Bank] ("Bank")
Account(s): See Schedule A (Deposit Account Details)
Governing Credit Agreement: Senior Secured Credit Agreement dated [●] (the "Credit Agreement")
Base Comparison Set: Internal ACA Playbook (Firm Standard); Executed Credit Agreement (Collateral / Control Provisions); Bank Standard Form ACA; Account Opening / Control Checklist; Deal Correspondence (controlling partner instruction); Schedules 3.7 & 5.2; Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)

Legend (textual tracked changes):
  [DELETE: text] = deletion from counterparty draft
  [INSERT: text] = insertion required by playbook / Credit Agreement / Bank form / client instruction
  [MOVE] / comments in braces {Comment: …} = drafting notes for negotiation

================================================================================
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
================================================================================

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of [●], 20[●] (the "Effective Date"), by and among:

(i) [DEBTOR LEGAL NAME], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Debtor");
(ii) [ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT NAME], as Administrative Agent for the Lenders party to the Credit Agreement described below (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns in such capacity, the "Secured Party"); and
(iii) [DEPOSITORY BANK LEGAL NAME] (the "Bank").

RECITALS

A. The Debtor and the Secured Party are parties to that certain Senior Secured Credit Agreement dated as of [●] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement"), pursuant to which the Debtor has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Accounts (as defined below).

B. The Debtor maintains with the Bank the deposit account(s) identified on Schedule A attached hereto (each, a "Deposit Account" and collectively, the "Deposit Accounts").

C. The parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party's security interest in the Deposit Accounts by "control" under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the "UCC"), and to set forth the rights and obligations of the parties with respect to the Deposit Accounts.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 1.1 Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings ascribed in the Credit Agreement. As used in this Agreement:

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York [INSERT: or the city in which the Bank's office maintaining the Deposit Accounts is located] are authorized or required by law to close.

"Control Notice" means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit C (or such other form as the Bank and Secured Party may reasonably agree), stating that the Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Deposit Accounts.

[INSERT: "Excluded Amounts" means amounts on deposit in a Deposit Account that constitute (i) trust or escrow funds held solely for the benefit of third parties and identified as such in writing to the Bank and the Secured Party, or (ii) amounts required by Applicable Law to be maintained in a segregated account for the benefit of employees or taxing authorities, in each case only to the extent and for so long as such amounts are so held.]

"Indemnified Liabilities" has the meaning set forth in Section 7.1.

[INSERT: "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities (actual or contingent), operations, condition (financial or otherwise) or prospects of the Debtor and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, (b) the ability of the Debtor to perform any of its obligations under this Agreement or the other Loan Documents, (c) the legality, validity, binding effect or enforceability against the Debtor of this Agreement or any other Loan Document to which it is a party, or (d) the rights, remedies and benefits available to, or conferred upon, the Secured Party under this Agreement or any other Loan Document; [DELETE: provided, however, that "Material Adverse Effect" shall exclude any effect arising from or relating to (x) any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination or proceeding by any Governmental Authority, or (y) any change in Applicable Law or the interpretation or enforcement thereof]. {Comment: Counterparty MAE regulatory carve-outs REJECTED — playbook non-waivable; Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries make carve-out particularly harmful. Restore Credit Agreement-aligned MAE without regulatory carve-outs.}]

"Notice of Exclusive Control" has the meaning given to Control Notice.

"Obligations" means all obligations of the Debtor under the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents, whether now existing or hereafter arising.

[INSERT: "Permitted Free Disposition Period" means the period commencing on the Effective Date and ending on the earlier of (i) the date the Bank receives a Control Notice and (ii) the date this Agreement terminates in accordance with its terms.]

"UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect from time to time in the State of New York; provided that if by reason of mandatory provisions of law, perfection, the effect of perfection or non-perfection, or priority of the security interest is governed by the UCC as in effect in a jurisdiction other than New York, "UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in such other jurisdiction for purposes of the provisions hereof relating to such perfection, effect of perfection or non-perfection, or priority.

Section 1.2 UCC Terms. Terms defined in Article 8 or 9 of the UCC and not otherwise defined herein have the meanings ascribed therein (including "authenticate," "control," "deposit account," "entitlement holder," "financial asset," "proceeds," and "securities intermediary").

Section 1.3 Rules of Construction. The rules of construction set forth in the Credit Agreement apply mutatis mutandis to this Agreement. References to "including" mean "including without limitation." Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE II — THE DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS; ESTABLISHMENT OF CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 2.1 Identification of Deposit Accounts. The Debtor represents and warrants that Schedule A completely and accurately identifies each Deposit Account subject to this Agreement, including account number, account title, account type, and the Bank office at which each Deposit Account is maintained. [INSERT: The Debtor shall not open, maintain, or permit to exist any other deposit account with the Bank that is required to be subject to an account control agreement under the Credit Agreement unless such account is added to Schedule A by a written supplement executed by the Debtor, the Secured Party, and the Bank.] {Comment: Playbook / Credit Agreement covenant alignment — all required accounts must be covered.}

Section 2.2 Acknowledgment of Security Interest. The Debtor hereby confirms that it has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in the Deposit Accounts and all cash, checks, wire transfers, and other items at any time on deposit therein or credited thereto, and all proceeds thereof (collectively, the "Collateral"), pursuant to the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents. The Bank acknowledges that it has received notice of such security interest.

Section 2.3 Control. The parties agree that this Agreement provides the Secured Party with "control" of each Deposit Account within the meaning of Sections 9-104 and, to the extent applicable, 8-106 of the UCC. Without limiting the foregoing:
  (a) the Bank will comply with all instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Deposit Accounts without further consent by the Debtor;
  (b) [INSERT: the Bank subordinates any security interest, lien, right of setoff, or recoupment it may have in or against the Deposit Accounts and the Collateral to the security interest of the Secured Party, except for the Bank's rights expressly preserved under Section 5.3 (Permitted Bank Claims);] and
  (c) the Bank shall not agree with any third party to comply with instructions concerning the Deposit Accounts originated by such third party without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.

Section 2.4 [INSERT: No Other Control Agreements. The Bank represents that, as of the Effective Date, it has not entered into any other agreement with any person (other than the Debtor in the ordinary course regarding account operation) to comply with instructions concerning any Deposit Account originated by a person other than the Debtor or the Secured Party. The Bank agrees that it will not enter into any such agreement without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.] {Comment: Bank standard form / playbook required representation.}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE III — OPERATION OF DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS PRIOR TO CONTROL NOTICE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 3.1 Debtor's Access Prior to Control Notice. Until the Bank receives a Control Notice from the Secured Party:
  (a) the Bank may permit the Debtor to operate and make withdrawals from, and otherwise give instructions concerning, the Deposit Accounts in accordance with the Bank's standard account documentation and past practice, subject to the terms of this Agreement and the Credit Agreement;
  (b) the Bank shall have no duty to inquire into the purpose of any instruction from the Debtor or whether any withdrawal is permitted under the Credit Agreement; and
  (c) [INSERT: the Debtor shall not close any Deposit Account, change the account title or account number in a manner that would impair perfection or priority, or transfer any Deposit Account to another office of the Bank or to another depository institution, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party (not to be unreasonably withheld with respect to office transfers within the Bank that preserve control).]

Section 3.2 Account Statements; Information. The Bank shall send to the Secured Party, at the address set forth in Section 8.1 (or such other address as the Secured Party may designate), copies of all account statements, debit and credit advices, and other account information with respect to the Deposit Accounts that the Bank sends to the Debtor, [INSERT: concurrently with delivery to the Debtor, and shall provide the Secured Party online view-only access to the Deposit Accounts upon reasonable request and completion of the Bank's customary access procedures]. The Debtor authorizes the Bank to provide such information and access to the Secured Party without further consent.

Section 3.3 [INSERT: Automated Sweep / Investment Features. Any automated sweep, investment, or zero-balance arrangement affecting a Deposit Account shall be disclosed on Schedule A. The Debtor shall not implement any new sweep or investment feature without prior written notice to the Secured Party and confirmation that control is preserved. Upon receipt of a Control Notice, all sweep and investment features shall be suspended unless the Secured Party otherwise directs in writing.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE IV — EXERCISE OF CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 4.1 Control Notice. At any time the Secured Party may deliver a Control Notice to the Bank. The Control Notice shall be effective upon the Bank's actual receipt during Business Day hours at the notice address in Section 8.1 (or, if received after such hours or on a non-Business Day, at the opening of the next Business Day). [INSERT: The Secured Party shall concurrently send a copy of the Control Notice to the Debtor at the notice address in Section 8.1; provided that failure to so copy the Debtor shall not affect the validity or effectiveness of the Control Notice as against the Bank or the Debtor's obligations hereunder.]

Section 4.2 Effect of Control Notice. From and after the effectiveness of a Control Notice:
  (a) the Bank shall not permit any withdrawal, transfer, or other disposition of funds from any Deposit Account except solely upon the written instructions of the Secured Party (including standing instructions);
  (b) the Bank shall cease complying with instructions originated by the Debtor with respect to the disposition of funds in the Deposit Accounts;
  (c) the Bank shall comply with instructions originated by the Secured Party concerning the Deposit Accounts without further consent by the Debtor; and
  (d) [INSERT: the Bank shall, within one (1) Business Day after effectiveness of the Control Notice, confirm in writing to the Secured Party (with a copy to the Debtor) that the Control Notice has been received and implemented.]

Section 4.3 [INSERT: Partial / Modified Instructions. The Secured Party may revoke, modify, or replace a Control Notice or any instruction by subsequent authenticated writing to the Bank. The Bank may rely on the most recent authenticated instruction received from the Secured Party.]

Section 4.4 No Duty to Inquire. The Bank shall have no duty to inquire whether an Event of Default (or any other condition) under the Credit Agreement has occurred or whether the Secured Party is entitled, under the Credit Agreement or Applicable Law, to deliver a Control Notice or any instruction. [INSERT: The Bank may conclusively rely on any Control Notice or instruction that the Bank reasonably believes in good faith to have been given by an authorized person of the Secured Party.]

Section 4.5 [INSERT: Rescission Only by Secured Party. The Debtor shall have no right to rescind a Control Notice or to reinstate Debtor operational authority over the Deposit Accounts except with the prior written consent of the Secured Party delivered to the Bank.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE V — BANK'S RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS; SUBORDINATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 5.1 Limited Duties. The Bank undertakes to perform only such duties as are expressly set forth herein and in the UCC with respect to control. The Bank shall not be deemed a fiduciary for the Secured Party or the Debtor by reason of this Agreement. [INSERT: The Bank shall exercise the same degree of care in administering the Deposit Accounts as it exercises with respect to similar accounts maintained for its other customers, but in no event less than reasonable care.]

Section 5.2 No Obligation to Extend Credit. Nothing in this Agreement obligates the Bank to extend credit, honor overdrafts, or permit the Deposit Accounts to have a negative balance.

Section 5.3 Permitted Bank Claims. Notwithstanding Section 2.3(b), the Bank may exercise rights of setoff, recoupment, or banker's lien against the Deposit Accounts solely with respect to:
  (a) the face amount of items deposited to a Deposit Account and returned unpaid;
  (b) ordinary account fees, charges, and expenses of the Bank for maintaining and operating the Deposit Accounts in accordance with the Bank's published fee schedule (or as otherwise agreed in writing);
  (c) [INSERT: overdrafts and related reasonable charges arising in the ordinary course prior to the Bank's receipt of a Control Notice, not to exceed $[●] in the aggregate without the Secured Party's prior written consent;] and
  (d) the Bank's reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred in complying with this Agreement or any Control Notice or legal process relating to the Deposit Accounts,
in each case subject to the priority arrangements in Section 5.4. [DELETE: The Bank retains all rights of setoff and recoupment against the Deposit Accounts for any and all obligations of the Debtor to the Bank, whether now existing or hereafter arising, including credit facilities, derivatives, and treasury services exposures.] {Comment: Open-ended Bank setoff REJECTED — playbook and Credit Agreement require narrow, specified Permitted Bank Claims only.}

Section 5.4 Priority; Turnover. The Bank's Permitted Bank Claims under Section 5.3 shall have priority over the Secured Party's security interest solely to the extent of such Permitted Bank Claims. [INSERT: If the Bank receives or applies funds in respect of any claim that is not a Permitted Bank Claim after notice of the Secured Party's security interest, the Bank shall hold such funds in trust for the Secured Party and promptly turn them over to the Secured Party upon demand.] After receipt of a Control Notice, the Bank shall not exercise setoff or recoupment against the Deposit Accounts other than for items described in Section 5.3(a), (b), and (d) without the Secured Party's prior written consent.

Section 5.5 Legal Process. If the Bank receives any levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process with respect to any Deposit Account, the Bank shall [INSERT: promptly (and in any event within two (2) Business Days)] notify the Secured Party and the Debtor, and may comply with such legal process to the extent required by Applicable Law. [INSERT: Compliance with legal process shall not, by itself, terminate control or this Agreement.]

Section 5.6 Resignation; Successor Bank. The Bank may resign as depository bank with respect to the Deposit Accounts upon [DELETE: ten (10)] [INSERT: thirty (30)] days' prior written notice to the Debtor and the Secured Party; provided that such resignation shall not become effective until a successor depository bank reasonably acceptable to the Secured Party has executed an account control agreement in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Secured Party with respect to replacement deposit accounts, and the funds have been transferred. [INSERT: The Debtor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts and obtain an acceptable control agreement prior to the effectiveness of resignation.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE VI — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 6.1 Debtor Representations. The Debtor represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank as of the Effective Date [INSERT: and on each date on which any funds are deposited to a Deposit Account] that:
  (a) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization;
  (b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
  (c) this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered and constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy and equitable principles;
  (d) the execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with its organizational documents, any material agreement binding upon it, or any Applicable Law [INSERT: in any manner that could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect];
  (e) it is the sole entitlement holder / customer with respect to each Deposit Account, and no other person has a controlling interest or "control" (as defined in the UCC) over any Deposit Account except the Secured Party pursuant to this Agreement;
  (f) [INSERT: except as set forth on Schedule 3.7 (Pending Regulatory Inquiries), there is no pending or, to the Debtor's knowledge, threatened action, suit, investigation, or proceeding before any Governmental Authority that could reasonably be expected to materially and adversely affect the Deposit Accounts, the Collateral, or the Debtor's ability to perform under this Agreement;] {Comment: Align with Schedule 3.7 disclosure; do NOT convert disclosure into MAE carve-out.}
  (g) Schedule A is true, complete, and correct; and
  (h) [INSERT: the security interest granted in the Collateral has been duly authorized and, upon execution of this Agreement, the Secured Party will have a perfected security interest in the Deposit Accounts by control, senior in priority to all other liens other than Permitted Bank Claims.]

Section 6.2 Bank Representations. The Bank represents and warrants as of the Effective Date that:
  (a) it is a [bank / "bank" as defined in UCC §9-102] organized under the laws of [●] and is acting in that capacity with respect to the Deposit Accounts;
  (b) the officer executing this Agreement is duly authorized to do so;
  (c) [INSERT: each Deposit Account is a "deposit account" as defined in UCC §9-102];
  (d) [INSERT: the jurisdiction of the Bank for purposes of UCC §§9-304 and 9-305 is the State of [●] (and the Bank will not change such jurisdiction without at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Secured Party)]; and
  (e) the acknowledgments and agreements of the Bank herein are irrevocable prior to termination of this Agreement in accordance with its terms.

Section 6.3 Secured Party Representation. The Secured Party represents that the officer executing this Agreement on its behalf is duly authorized to do so [INSERT: and that it is the Administrative Agent under the Credit Agreement with authority to enter into this Agreement for the benefit of the Secured Parties thereunder].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE VII — INDEMNIFICATION; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY; SURVIVAL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 7.1 Indemnification by Debtor. The Debtor agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Bank and the Secured Party, and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and advisors (each, an "Indemnified Person"), from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys' fees and expenses) (collectively, "Indemnified Liabilities") arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Deposit Accounts, or any action taken or omitted by an Indemnified Person pursuant to this Agreement, EXCEPT to the extent resulting from such Indemnified Person's [DELETE: gross negligence or willful misconduct] [INSERT: gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of this Agreement, in each case as determined by a final non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction].

Section 7.2 Indemnification Cap and Basket.
  (a) Cap. The Debtor's aggregate liability under Section 7.1 to the Bank shall not exceed [DELETE: an amount equal to fifty percent (50%) of] [INSERT: an amount equal to] the average daily aggregate balance of the Deposit Accounts during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim (or, if shorter, the period since the Effective Date), [INSERT: provided that the foregoing cap shall not apply to Indemnified Liabilities arising from (i) the Debtor's fraud or willful misconduct, (ii) the Debtor's failure to pay ordinary Bank fees when due, or (iii) third-party claims resulting from the Debtor's breach of Applicable Law]. {Comment: Silent reduction of indemnification cap REJECTED — restore full playbook / Bank-form cap without 50% haircut; retain standard carve-outs from cap.}
  (b) Basket. [DELETE: No indemnification claim may be made unless and until the aggregate amount of Indemnified Liabilities exceeds $[●] (the "Basket"), in which event the Indemnified Person may recover the full amount of Indemnified Liabilities including amounts within the Basket (a "tipping basket").] [INSERT: No indemnification claim may be made by the Bank against the Debtor under Section 7.1 unless and until the aggregate amount of Indemnified Liabilities exceeds $[●] (the "Basket"), and the Bank may recover only the amount of Indemnified Liabilities in excess of the Basket (a "deductible basket"); provided, solely as a negotiated commercial concession per controlling deal-team instruction, the parties may implement a tipping-basket mechanic under which, once the Basket is exceeded, recoverable Indemnified Liabilities include amounts within the Basket. For the avoidance of doubt, the Basket shall not apply to ordinary account fees or to claims based on fraud or willful misconduct.] {Comment: Per controlling partner correspondence, CLIENT CONCEDES basket conversion from deductible to tipping. Redline implements tipping basket as acceptable fallback while preserving fraud/willful-misconduct and fee carve-outs. Preferred playbook position remains deductible; tipping accepted as commercial compromise only.}
  (c) [INSERT: Interaction with Schedule 5.2. Nothing in this Article VII shall be construed to shift to the Secured Party or to release the Debtor from any retained liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities). The indemnification modifications in the counterparty draft that would have silently reallocated Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are rejected. Schedule 5.2 controls.]

Section 7.3 Bank Limitation of Liability. The Bank shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted in good faith in connection with this Agreement, except to the extent resulting from the Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct as determined by a final non-appealable judgment. [INSERT: In no event shall the Bank be liable for special, indirect, consequential, or punitive damages, whether or not foreseeable, except to the extent awarded to a third party in a claim for which the Bank is entitled to indemnification and as to which the Debtor's indemnity applies.] The Bank shall be entitled to rely on, and shall not be liable for acting or refraining from acting upon, any notice, instruction, or document believed by it in good faith to be genuine and to have been signed or sent by the proper person.

Section 7.4 Secured Party Limitation. The Secured Party shall not be liable to the Bank or the Debtor for any action taken or omitted in good faith under this Agreement, except to the extent of its own gross negligence or willful misconduct as determined by a final non-appealable judgment. The Secured Party shall have no duty to supervise the Debtor's use of the Deposit Accounts prior to delivery of a Control Notice.

ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review

TO:      Deal Team / Partner
FROM:    Contracts Counsel
DATE:    [●]
RE:      Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement — Deviations, Missing Protections, Off-Market Terms, Risk Ratings, and Recommended Positions
MATTER:  Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
RELATED: aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline implementing required modifications)

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("ACA") against: (1) the firm's internal ACA playbook; (2) the executed Senior Secured Credit Agreement (collateral and cash-control provisions); (3) the depository bank's standard form ACA; (4) account details and the account-control checklist; (5) Schedules 3.7 (Pending Regulatory Inquiries) and 5.2 (Retained Liabilities) and Exhibit B (Survival Matrix); and (6) deal-team correspondence, of which the latest partner instruction controls.

Primary counterparty deviations (also flagged in the counterparty markup file):
  (A) Silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
  (B) Material Adverse Effect definition expanded with regulatory-action carve-outs that intersect Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries;
  (C) New contractual limitation period shortening survival for core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner correspondence — supersedes earlier opposite priority ordering):
  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): CLIENT WILL CONCEDE.
  • Any survival-period reduction: WALK-AWAY ISSUE.

Additional material gaps versus playbook / Credit Agreement / Bank form include open-ended Bank setoff, missing control-confirmation and information-rights mechanics, weak subordination/turnover language, inadequate account-coverage covenants, and missing UCC jurisdiction and "no other control agreement" Bank representations.

The companion redline (aca-redline.docx) implements all required deletions, restorations, and insertions. This memorandum identifies every deviation and missing protection with section references, playbook requirements, risk ratings, exposure analysis, and recommended positions, and closes with a summary deviation matrix.

Risk Rating Scale:
  CRITICAL — Walk-away / non-waivable without partner + client written approval
  HIGH     — Material economic or perfection/priority risk; push hard; escalate if resisted
  MEDIUM   — Meaningful but negotiable; tradeable against wins on CRITICAL/HIGH
  LOW      — Cleanup, conformity, or optional enhancement

================================================================================
II. SCOPE OF REVIEW AND SOURCE HIERARCHY
================================================================================

Documents and materials reviewed:
  1. Counterparty draft ACA (base paper under review)
  2. Internal ACA Playbook (firm standard positions and non-waivables)
  3. Executed Credit Agreement — deposit account, cash management, collateral, and control provisions
  4. Depository Bank standard form ACA
  5. Account details / control checklist (account inventory, sweep features, office/ABA)
  6. Schedule 3.7 — Pending Regulatory Inquiries (two inquiries)
  7. Schedule 5.2 — Retained Liabilities
  8. Exhibit B — Survival Matrix
  9. Deal-team correspondence (latest partner email controls; earlier opposite priority ordering is superseded)

Source hierarchy applied in the redline and this memo:
  (i)   Controlling deal-team instruction (latest) on basket vs. survival
  (ii)  Credit Agreement (as between Debtor and Secured Party)
  (iii) Exhibit B and Schedules 3.7 / 5.2 (scheduled exceptions control over general body text)
  (iv)  Internal ACA Playbook non-waivables (perfection/control, subordination, survival fundamentals)
  (v)  Bank standard form (operational mechanics acceptable if control/priority preserved)
  (vi) Counterparty draft (accepted only where consistent with (i)–(v))

================================================================================
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §7.2(a) (Indemnification Cap)
Counterparty text:  Cap set at fifty percent (50%) of average daily aggregate Deposit Account balances over trailing twelve months.
Playbook / Bank form / Credit Agreement requirement:
  Full (100%) average-daily-balance cap (or other playbook metric), with standard carve-outs from the cap for Debtor fraud/willful misconduct, unpaid ordinary Bank fees, and third-party claims from Debtor's breach of Applicable Law. Silent haircuts are non-market on lender/Bank paper.
Risk Rating:        HIGH
Exposure Analysis:  A 50% silent haircut halves recoveries available to the Bank (and, indirectly, pressures the Secured Party relationship and willingness of the Bank to act on Control Notices). On a Deposit Account complex averaging $20mm, exposure differential is ~$10mm of indemnity capacity. Also creates mismatch with Bank standard form, inviting Bank pushback or side-letter complexity. Interacts with Issue 2 (basket) and Issue 3 (Schedule 5.2 shift).
Recommended Position:
  REJECT the 50% reduction. Restore full average-daily-balance cap and express carve-outs from the cap. Not on the client's concession list. See redline §7.2(a).
Fallback:           If commercially necessary, floor the cap at the greater of (x) 100% of average daily balances and (y) a fixed dollar floor tied to expected peak cash; do not accept a percentage haircut without client approval.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 2 — Indemnification Basket Converted from Deductible to Tipping
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §7.2(b) (Basket)
Counterparty text:  Tipping basket — once threshold exceeded, Indemnified Person recovers full amount including amounts within the Basket.
Playbook requirement:
  Deductible basket (recover only excess over Basket); Basket inapplicable to ordinary fees and fraud/willful misconduct.
Controlling client instruction:
  CLIENT WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion (latest partner correspondence). Earlier messages stating the opposite priority are superseded.
Risk Rating:        MEDIUM (elevated only by interaction with cap and Schedule 5.2; commercially conceded)
Exposure Analysis:  Tipping vs. deductible increases Debtor's expected indemnity outlay by up to the Basket amount per qualifying claim series. Quantum depends on negotiated Basket. Secondary risk: if combined with reduced cap (Issue 1) and silent Schedule 5.2 shift (Issue 3), cumulative economics move materially off-market.
Recommended Position:
  ACCEPT tipping-basket mechanic as commercial concession per controlling instruction. Preserve: (i) Basket inapplicable to ordinary Bank fees and fraud/willful misconduct; (ii) no application of basket mechanics to reallocate Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; (iii) do not trade this concession for any survival cut (Issue 5). Implement in redline §7.2(b) with express notation that preferred playbook position remains deductible.
Negotiation note:   Document the concession expressly so it is not re-opened; pair acceptance with insistence on Issues 1, 3, and 5.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 3 — Silent Shift of Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities via Indemnity Changes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §7.2 / Article VII generally; Schedule 5.2
Counterparty effect: Indemnification cap/basket rewrite would silently reallocate retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2.
Playbook / schedules requirement:
  Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain with Debtor; indemnity mechanics may not override scheduled retained liabilities. Scheduled exceptions control over general body statements.
Risk Rating:        HIGH
Exposure Analysis:  Retained liabilities (e.g., specified pre-closing taxes, identified litigation, environmental) can be individually material. Silent reallocation through indemnity drafting is a classic hidden transfer of economic risk and undermines the negotiated disclosure schedule architecture.
Recommended Position:
  REJECT any reading or drafting that shifts Schedule 5.2 items. Insert express override: "Nothing in Article VII shall be construed to shift to the Secured Party or to release the Debtor from any retained liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2. Schedule 5.2 controls." See redline §7.2(c) and Schedule 5.2 legend.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 4 — Material Adverse Effect Definition — Regulatory Carve-Outs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §1.1 (Definition of Material Adverse Effect); interacts with §6.1(d), (f)
Counterparty text:  MAE excludes effects arising from (x) any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination, or proceeding by any Governmental Authority, or (y) any change in Applicable Law or interpretation/enforcement.
Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
  MAE aligned to Credit Agreement — no broad regulatory-action carve-out. Pending or threatened regulatory matters are handled by specific disclosure (Schedule 3.7), not by gutting MAE.
Schedule 3.7 intersection:
  Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that sit squarely inside the counterparty's proposed carve-outs. Permitting the carve-out would nullify MAE protection precisely where known risk exists.
Risk Rating:        HIGH (CRITICAL if ACA MAE is cross-referenced into remedial triggers; otherwise HIGH)
Exposure Analysis:  With two live regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7, a regulatory carve-out would prevent MAE from being triggered by escalation, adverse findings, or material operational restrictions arising from those exact matters. That is the paradigm case of an off-market, deal-specific giveaway. Also creates Credit Agreement vs. ACA definitional inconsistency, impairing integrated enforcement.
Recommended Position:
  REJECT regulatory carve-outs in full. Restore Credit Agreement-aligned MAE. Permit disclosure-only qualification via Schedule 3.7 to the §6.1(f) representation; do not convert disclosure into an MAE carve-out. See redline §1.1 MAE and §6.1(f).
Fallback:           At most, a narrow forward-looking carve-out for generally applicable law changes not disproportionately affecting the Debtor — still no carve-out for inquiries/investigations/proceedings, and no carve-out covering Schedule 3.7 matters.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 5 — Survival Period Shortened for Core Representations (WALK-AWAY)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §7.5 (Survival); Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)
Counterparty text:  Flat twelve (12) month post-termination survival for representations / related claims.
Playbook / Exhibit B requirement:
  Exhibit B survival matrix controls:
    • Fundamental reps (organization, authority, enforceability, sole customer status, creation/perfection of security interest): indefinite / applicable statute of limitations
    • Other Article VI reps: thirty-six (36) months post-termination
    • Indemnification: applicable statute of limitations + 60 days
  Exhibit B controls over conflicting body text.
Controlling client instruction:
  ANY SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION IS A WALK-AWAY ISSUE. Latest partner correspondence expressly revises priorities: concede basket; do not concede survival. Earlier opposite ordering is superseded and must not be followed.
Risk Rating:        CRITICAL
Exposure Analysis:  A 12-month wrap-up on fundamental reps (including perfection/control and sole-customer status) would extinguish claims before many latent perfection, priority, or fraudulent-transfer issues surface — especially in enforcement, bankruptcy, or Bank-error scenarios. Directly contradicts Exhibit B. Accepting this term would be off-market for secured-lending ACAs and inconsistent with Credit Agreement collateral package durability.
Recommended Position:
  REJECT IN FULL. Restore Exhibit B matrix. Insert body-text override that Exhibit B controls and that any contractual limitation period shortening fundamental-rep or indemnity survival below Exhibit B is void. Do not trade survival for basket, cap, or any other concession. See redline §7.5(a)–(c) and Exhibit B.
Escalation:         If counterparty insists, escalate immediately to partner/client as walk-away; do not continue to signature.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 6 — Open-Ended Bank Setoff / Recoupment
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §5.3 (Permitted Bank Claims); §5.4 (Priority; Turnover)
Counterparty text:  Bank retains all rights of setoff and recoupment for any and all obligations of Debtor to Bank, now existing or hereafter arising, including credit facilities, derivatives, and treasury services.
Playbook / Credit Agreement / Bank form (lender-acceptable) requirement:
  Narrow, enumerated Permitted Bank Claims only: returned items; ordinary account fees; limited ordinary-course overdrafts (capped); reasonable compliance costs. Express subordination of all other Bank liens/setoff to Secured Party. Post-Control Notice setoff freeze except returned items/fees/compliance costs. Turnover trust language for non-permitted applications.
Risk Rating:        HIGH (CRITICAL to perfection/priority integrity if Bank has material other exposures)
Exposure Analysis:  Open-ended setoff can prime the Secured Party on the entire cash collateral pool up to the Bank's full cross-exposure (revolver, cards, FX, swaps, TMS). In a distress scenario this can erase years of cash dominion structuring. Off-market versus institutional ACA practice and inconsistent with Credit Agreement first-priority collateral requirements.
Recommended Position:
  REJECT open-ended setoff. Replace with enumerated Permitted Bank Claims, subordination, post-notice freeze, and turnover trust. See redline §§2.3(b), 5.3, 5.4.
Fallback:           Limited additional Bank product exposure only if (i) capped, (ii) scheduled, (iii) expressly junior or pari only as playbook allows, and (iv) Credit Agreement permits.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 7 — Missing / Weak "Control" Operative Language and UCC Alignment
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §2.3 (Control); §4.1–4.5 (Exercise of Control); §6.2 (Bank reps)
Counterparty gaps:  Incomplete statement of UCC §9-104 control elements; no express Bank agreement to comply with Secured Party instructions without Debtor consent; weak or missing confirmation-of-implementation duty; no Debtor-rescission bar; missing Bank rep that each account is a "deposit account"; missing UCC jurisdiction rep and change-notice; missing "no other control agreement" rep.
Playbook / Bank form / checklist requirement:
  Express control under UCC §§9-104 / 8-106; Bank will comply with SP instructions without further Debtor consent; no third-party control agreements; deposit-account characterization; UCC jurisdiction locked with notice before change; Control Notice effectiveness mechanics; written implementation confirmation within one Business Day; only SP may rescind Control Notice; reliance standard for Bank.
Risk Rating:        HIGH (perfection foundation)
Exposure Analysis:  Ambiguity on control elements invites priority contests by lien creditors, bankruptcy trustees, and competing secured parties. Missing jurisdiction lock creates unexpected choice-of-law risk under UCC §§9-304/9-305. Absence of "no other control agreement" rep leaves open a dual-control conflict.
Recommended Position:
  INSERT full playbook control package: §§2.3, 2.4, 4.1–4.5, 6.2(c)–(e), Exhibit C form of Control Notice. Non-waivable foundation terms.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 8 — Account Coverage, Sweeps, and Post-Closing Account Controls
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §2.1, §3.1(c), §3.3, Schedule A, Exhibit D
Counterparty gaps:  No covenant to add newly required accounts; no restriction on closing/retitling/moving accounts; no sweep/ZBA disclosure or freeze-on-control; no joinder form for added accounts; Schedule A incomplete relative to checklist.
Playbook / Credit Agreement / checklist requirement:
  All Credit Agreement-required accounts at the Bank listed on Schedule A; mandatory joinder before opening additional required accounts; no close/retitle/transfer without SP consent; sweep features disclosed and suspended on Control Notice; Debtor certification of completeness.
Risk Rating:        HIGH
Exposure Analysis:  Ungoverned new accounts and undisclosed sweeps are common perfection leaks. Cash can migrate outside controlled accounts within a single Business Day. Credit Agreement cash-management covenants are undermined if the ACA does not operationalize them at the Bank.
Recommended Position:
  INSERT coverage covenant (§2.1), anti-close/retitle (§3.1(c)), sweep controls (§3.3), Schedule A certification, and Exhibit D joinder. Conform Schedule A to checklist inventory before signing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 9 — Information Rights and Concurrent Statements
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §3.2
Counterparty gaps:  Statements to SP not expressly concurrent; no online view-only access; weak Debtor authorization language.
Playbook / Bank form requirement:
  Concurrent delivery of statements/advises to SP; online view-only access upon customary onboarding; standing Debtor authorization to Bank.
Risk Rating:        MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:  Delayed visibility impairs monitoring of cash dominion, borrowing-base, and early distress signals. Low drafting cost to fix.
Recommended Position:
  INSERT concurrent delivery + view-only access + standing authorization. See redline §3.2.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 10 — Bank Resignation Notice Period and Successor Conditionality
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §5.6
Counterparty text:  Ten (10) days' resignation notice; successor mechanics thin or absent.
Playbook / Bank form (lender-acceptable) requirement:
  At least thirty (30) days' prior written notice; resignation not effective until successor bank acceptable to SP has executed a satisfactory ACA and funds have moved; Debtor commercially reasonable efforts covenant.
Risk Rating:        MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:  A 10-day unconditioned exit can leave a control gap mid-enforcement or during refinancing. Successor conditionality is standard.
Recommended Position:
  Restore 30-day notice + effectiveness conditioned on successor ACA and fund transfer; add Debtor efforts covenant. See redline §5.6.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 11 — Legal Process Notification Timing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §5.5
Counterparty gaps:  No promptness standard; no statement that compliance with legal process does not itself terminate control.
Playbook requirement:
  Prompt notice (e.g., within two Business Days); control continuity clarification.
Risk Rating:        MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:  Levy/garnishment without prompt SP notice can drain controlled cash before SP can intervene.
Recommended Position:
  INSERT two-Business-Day notice and continuity clarification. See redline §5.5.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 12 — Indemnity Standard, Cap Carve-Outs, and Mutual Limitation of Liability
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):     §§7.1, 7.3, 7.4
